source.title: Probabilistic bounds on neuron death in deep rectifier networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and numerically tests bounds on whether randomly initialized ReLU networks remain alive, a trainability prerequisite related to the claim, but it measures initialization survival rather than training classification error.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own random-initialization simulations and sign-flipping/batch-normalization comparison. Cited findings about other work and architecture implications not measured in the study are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures neuron and data survival at initialization, not training error, learning speed, trainable depth demonstrated through training, or learning-rate tolerance. These are related prerequisites rather than the outcomes named by V1–V6. Its architectural explanations do not establish any version's training effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors derive width- and depth-dependent survival bounds, report simulation agreement and evidence of lower-bound tightness, and propose sign-flipping to preserve living data. They also report the stated batch-normalization result. They explicitly restrict the study to initialization and do not claim neuron death completely explains training efficacy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies random initialization survival and neuron death, not optimization to classification error or the claim’s training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Network width and depth, initialization distribution, and initialization scheme (IID, sign-flipping, batch normalization) affect the reported survival measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Random ReLU network survival depends on width and depth; simulations agree with the theoretical bounds and approach the lower bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width and depth constrain the probability of a living ReLU initialization, without establishing successful subsequent optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-dependent sign-flipping substantially increases living-data proportion over IID initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sign-flipping initialization can preserve more living input data in ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch normalization prevents total network death in the tested simulations but does not increase living-data proportion over the IID baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preventing total network death at initialization need not improve the fraction of living data.

record.problems: The reported numerical results are presented in figures without tabulated values or uncertainty estimates. The simulations use fully connected ReLU networks and random Gaussian data; they do not measure classification training error. The asymptotic lower-bound argument depends on an output-variance assumption that the authors say is not established by their experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. Theoretical bounds and the random-network simulation are represented; architecture discussion about residual connections and skip connections is not an empirical result of this study.

untested.parts: Training classification error under SGD or Adam, CIFAR datasets, corrupted labels, and model-size or regularization effects.
Teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima, and the effects of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training error and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special initialization, or Fixup.
Learning speed and successful training depth across initialization schemes; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, divergence, and sharpness during training.
Faster accuracy gains, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free training performance.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V6 limits_scope verdict: an unchanged initialization-survival measure does not qualify the version's training-performance claim. Section 6 also says the normalized-variance decay required by Assumption 5.6 was not observed; the general tightness argument remains conditional.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, SGD or Adam training, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random labels, model size effects on training, and early stopping.
Teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Training error across depth, plain versus residual shortcuts during training, and the cited special-initialization or Fixup training results.
Comparative training speed and trainable depth across initialization schemes; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness during training.
The paper compares batch normalization only on living-data proportion at initialization; it does not test faster accuracy gain, higher learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup.

rows.subject: IID
rows.size_stated: fully-connected ReLU networks; n ∈ {1, . . . , 15} features and 1 ≤ k ≤ 256 layers
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of living data under IID parameter initialization.

conditions.value: He initialization; multiplicative parameters normal with variance σθ2 = 2/n; additive parameters zero

rows.note: IID is the comparison baseline for sign-flipping and batch normalization. The paper states it matches the lower bound for IID data.
rows.check: Living-data probability at initialization cannot establish V6's accuracy gains or learning-rate tolerance. The IID baseline is a valid auxiliary measurement.

rows.subject: sign flipping
rows.size_stated: k-layer ReLU network; other dimensions as in Figure 6
rows.operation_detail: Negated a layer’s parameters when more than half of the previously living data points were killed.
rows.note: The text says sign-flipping significantly increased the living-data proportion, far exceeding the theoretical 2−k fraction guarantee.
rows.check: Sign-flipping increases living-data proportion according to section 7, but measures neither batch-normalization training benefits nor initialization-dependent training speed. The observed auxiliary improvement does not establish a claim-version effect.

rows.subject: batch norm
rows.size_stated: k-layer ReLU network; other dimensions as in Figure 6
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch normalization’s effect on living-data proportion against IID initialization.
rows.note: The paper says batch normalization ensured the network was alive but did not increase the living-data proportion over the IID baseline.
rows.check: The stated absence concerns improvement in living-data proportion over IID initialization. It does not show that batch normalization fails to accelerate training or increase learning-rate tolerance, so 'absent' is inappropriate for V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Living-data proportion at initialization under the tested ReLU network settings
reader_labels.reason: Batch normalization ensures a living network but does not increase living-data proportion over the IID baseline (R1, R3); the study does not test faster accuracy gain or tolerance of higher learning rates.
